metadata.note: Missouri Pacific's Missouri River Eagle, the historical predecessor of Amtrak's Missouri River Runner on the St. Louis-Kansas City corridor. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables. CORRECTION (2026-08-18): this line originally began in 1940 with the streamlined Missouri River Eagle, which wrongly left the St. Louis-Kansas City corridor blank for the entire 19th century. Segments now run back to the Pacific Railroad's Dec 9 1852 opening - the first railroad west of the Mississippi.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Missouri Pacific, Colorado Eagle), american-rails.com, corridorrail.com
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Ground was broken for the Pacific Railroad at St. Louis on Jul 4 1851, the nation's 75th birthday, and the first five miles from St. Louis to Cheltenham opened Dec 9 1852 - the first railroad to operate west of the Mississippi River. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Construction was interrupted by the Civil War; the line reached Kansas City in 1865, the first railroad to serve that city. Reorganized as the Missouri Pacific Railway in 1872. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Came under the control of New York financier Jay Gould in 1879, who built it into a system reaching Colorado, Nebraska, Arkansas, Texas and Louisiana. St. Louis Union Station opened Sept 1 1894 as the world's largest and busiest terminal, its train shed covering 30 tracks serving 22 railroads - the physical proof of how much rail converged here. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Inaugurated Mar 10 1940 simply as 'The Eagle', Missouri Pacific's first fast, streamlined, dieselized train, running daily each way St. Louis-Kansas City-Omaha. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Renamed the Missouri River Eagle in 1942 when the Colorado Eagle joined the fleet; it became the flagship of MoPac's Eagle streamliners. (This geometry shows the St. Louis-Kansas City portion now served by Amtrak; the Eagle continued north to Omaha.) Amtrak took over May 1 1971; the corridor is now the Missouri River Runner - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
